chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Stepfather teaches him the swamp and the snakes
summary: Chris Columbel taught him to hunt, fish and spot snakes in blackberry bushes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So you got all this music. You understand?

So my mother got a house and she got a husband. Mrs. Chris Columbel(?). Chris Columbel(?) knew everything you ever want to know about the swamp. You'd go out hunting and he'd come back with fish. You'd go out fishing and he'd come back with rabbits. He'd come back with alligator. He'd take me out in the woods with him. When we were walking in the woods, I'd get me a stick, and we'd make a steak right away. He'd tell us, 'Okay, now you watch, because you've got the snakes out here.' When we were going through the blackberries, he said, 'Watch them blackberry bushes. Snakes like blackberries. They get up in there, and they suck the juice.' And you'd see a bush, and you'd see all those blackberries that's been squashed, all of them ripe -- you'd watch that for snakes. He'd say, 'Watch over there. There's a snake over there. You see him?' I said, 'No, I don't see him.' He said, 'Look, you see by that yellow flower? You see his head over there? Look at it.' And sure enough, it's snake laying over there.
My grandmother told me about that blackberry thing. Boy, she went to pick a blackberry, and picked a snake up by the seed(?).
Yeah, they love... They go after the blackberries, because all of them are in the ground, and

they suck it in. Now, certainly the rock reptile is something else. They are very wise. That Bible scene, you know, where they say, "For doing what you did to Adam, you shall have your head stomped into the ground."
